details:
Mission Control is a browser game where you design a real space mission. You pick a target (the Moon, Mars or Europa) and how to meet it: a flyby, an orbiter or a lander. Then you build a spacecraft from 16 parts under six limits: budget, mass, power, data, comms and time. You find a launch window (Mars opens about every 26 months), watch your rocket launch, and make quick decisions when problems happen, like a solar flare or a dust storm. At the end a debrief explains why the mission worked or failed, shows other designs that also work, and compares your mission with the real NASA one (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter or Europa Clipper).

It is made for students with no space background. Every term is explained in plain words, and every part changes several numbers at once, so players feel the trade-offs of mission design. It has three difficulty levels, a sandbox mode with no budget limit, and English and Russian.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js (React Three Fiber), GSAP and Zustand. The rocket models are real NASA models, simplified in Blender and cut into stages. All game numbers (costs, masses, power, launch windows) are approximate values chosen for balance, not official figures.
